name: National Awami Party
role: Left-Nationalist Political Party in Pakistan and Bangladesh
contribution: The National Awami Party connected Maulana Bhashani's mass politics with anti-Ayub mobilization, autonomy demands, left-nationalist organizing, and later river-rights protest around Farakka.
context: East Pakistan opposition politics, the 1969 mass uprising, and post-independence Bangladesh's Farakka Long March politics.
impact: NAP broadened Bengali and East Pakistani opposition politics beyond Awami League constitutional nationalism, keeping peasant, left, and anti-imperial themes visible in mass movements.
highlight: A left-nationalist party associated with Bhashani's mass politics, anti-Ayub protest, and Farakka mobilization.
seoTitle: National Awami Party - East Bengal and Bangladesh Politics Profile
seoDescription: Profile of the National Awami Party, tracing Bhashani, anti-Ayub politics, the 1969 mass uprising, and Farakka Long March connections.
shortAnswer: National Awami Party was a left-nationalist party linked to Bhashani, anti-Ayub mass politics, and Farakka water-rights mobilization.

faq.question: Why does National Awami Party matter in Bengal history?
faq.answer: NAP linked left-nationalist politics, Bhashani's peasant-oriented mobilization, anti-Ayub protest, and later Farakka water-rights activism.
